title: What the filter is actually deciding

callouts.label: the whole decision is this one ratio
wheel slip breaks Q, so the filter trusts a wrong prediction

flow.step: Odometry carries the last estimate forward, and its uncertainty grows
A fix arrives, scattered but centred on the truth
The gain weighs the model's uncertainty against the sensor's
K near 1 believes the fix, K near 0 believes the model
The correction is K times the innovation, never all of it
The estimate lands between the two, more certain than either
It becomes the prior, and the cycle runs again

transcript.text: This is one cycle of a Kalman filter. It runs again for every fix that arrives.
Odometry carries the last estimate forward. Nothing has measured anything yet, so the filter is only less sure than it was.
Now a fix lands, and the innovation is the disagreement: what the fix says, minus what the model expected.
Here is the whole decision. The gain is the model's uncertainty over the total, so it asks which of the two is less sure right now.
K near 1 and the estimate jumps to the fix. K near 0 and it barely moves. Nothing asks which sensor is better in general.
The correction is K times the innovation, never the whole of it. That is why GPS jitter averages out instead of accumulating.
And the estimate ends up more certain than either input, which is the part that looks like magic and is really just two numbers.
Then it becomes the prior and the cycle runs again. Wheel slip breaks this: the odometry lies by more than Q admits, so the filter keeps believing a wrong prediction.
